record_used: subject f1y01 (young healthy adult), the first 5-minute RR window (391 RR intervals) -- the SAME git-tracked root the sibling Poincare (SD1/SD2) case uses. The cohort-consistency count uses all 10 subjects (5 young + 5 old).
pipeline: readRDS(rr5min_f1y01) -> PhysioECG::ecgHRVasymmetry (NEWLY-AUTHORED op): the heart-rate-asymmetry descriptors -- the Guzik/Slope/Area/Porta indices (GI/SI/AI/PI) and the deceleration/acceleration contributions to short-term (C1d/C1a), long-term (C2d/C2a), and total (Cd/Ca) HRV. The reference re-computes them with NeuroKit2 hrv_nonlinear (a bit-exact check of the newly-authored op; peaks reconstructed from the integer-ms RR at 250 Hz so NeuroKit2 sees the identical RR). Deterministic.
note: The tracked input is agent/eval/data/poincare-hrv/rr5min_f1y01.rds (the same 5-min f1y01 window the Poincare case uses). Heart-rate asymmetry (HRA; Guzik 2006, Piskorski & Guzik 2011) measures the Poincare plot's asymmetry about the line of identity: heart-rate DECELERATIONS (RR prolongations, points above the line) and ACCELERATIONS (shortenings, below) contribute unequally to variability -- a signature of vagal activity and of the temporal irreversibility of heart-rate dynamics. ecgHRVasymmetry is a NEW op authored to fill this gap (the ecosystem previously had only the symmetric SD1/SD2 via ecgHRVpoincare). It reproduces NeuroKit2's hrv_nonlinear HRA indices BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~1e-14 over all indices). The finding: decelerations contribute MORE than accelerations to short-term variability (C1d 0.63 > C1a 0.37), the established HRA signature, robust across the Fantasia cohort (8/10 subjects); accelerations dominate long-term variability (C2a 0.64 > C2d 0.36) on this subject, though the long-term asymmetry is weaker/mixed across the small cohort.
